name: n8n-code-javascript
description: Write JavaScript in n8n Code nodes using `$input`/`$json`/`$node`, `$helpers`, DateTime, and `$jmespath()`; troubleshoot errors and choose Code node modes.

## Modes and data
Choose "Run Once for All Items" mode (recommended for most use cases). It executes once; use `$input.all()` for aggregation, filtering, sorting, batch processing, and transformations. Choose "Run Once for Each Item" for independent, per-item logic; use `$input.item` or `$item`. Need to look at multiple items? Use "All Items" mode. Each item completely independent? Use "Each Item" mode. Not sure? Use "All Items" mode (you can always loop inside).

Access data with `$input.all()`, `$input.first()`, or `$input.item`. Use `$node["Webhook"].json` or `$node["HTTP Request"].json` for specific nodes. Webhook data is under `$json.body` (not `$json` directly); e.g. `$json.body.name` or `$input.first().json.body`.

## Output
Must return `[{json: {...}}]` format. Always return array of objects with `json` property. Example:
```js
return $input.all().map(item => ({json: item.json}));
```
Even empty results must use the array/object format. Do not return an object without the array wrapper, an array without `json`, a plain string, raw `$input.all()` without mapping, or `{data: value}`. Next nodes expect this format; invalid output can fail workflow execution. Always include a return statement; all code paths should return a consistent structure.

## Common patterns
```js
const items = $input.all();
const active = items.filter(item => item.json.status === 'active');
return active.map(item => ({json: {id: item.json.id}}));
```
For totals/statistics:
```js
const items = $input.all();
const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + (item.json.amount || 0), 0);
return [{json: {count: items.length, total, average: total / items.length}}];
```
Use `map`/`filter` over manual loops; filter before expensive transformations. Use clear variable names. Guard against missing/null data with optional chaining and guard clauses (e.g. `item.json?.user?.email`).

Do not use n8n expression syntax (`{{ }}`) in Code nodes; use JavaScript directly, e.g. `` `${$json.field}` ``. In other nodes, expressions use `{{ }}`.

HTTP:
```js
const response = await $helpers.httpRequest({
  url: 'https://api.example.com/data',
  headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer token', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
});
return [{json: {data: response}}];
```
Date/time: `DateTime.now()`, `.toFormat('yyyy-MM-dd')`, `.toISO()`, `.plus({days: 1})`, `.minus({weeks: 1})`.
JSON queries: `$jmespath(data, 'users[?age >= \`18\`]')`.

Use Code for complex transformations, calculations, business logic, parsing, conditionals, and aggregation. Prefer Set for simple field mapping, Filter for basic filtering, IF/Switch for simple conditionals, and HTTP Request for HTTP requests only. Debug with `console.log()`; statements appear in the browser console.

## n8n MCP Tools Expert
How to find Code node: `search_nodes({query: "code"})`
Get configuration help: `get_node_essentials("nodes-base.code")`
Validate code: `validate_node_operation()`
Can help select mode/language, understand property dependencies, build transformation and Webhook → Code → API workflows, handle and validate errors, and auto-fix common issues.

Before deploying Code nodes, verify:
[ ] **Code is not empty** - Must have meaningful logic
[ ] **Return statement exists** - Must return array of objects
[ ] **Proper return format** - Each item: `{json: {...}}`
[ ] **Data access correct** - Using `$input.all()`, `$input.first()`, or `$input.item`
[ ] **No n8n expressions** - Use JavaScript template literals: `` `${value}` ``
[ ] **Error handling** - Guard clauses for null/undefined inputs
[ ] **Webhook data** - Access via `.body` if from webhook
[ ] **Mode selection** - "All Items" for most cases
[ ] **Performance** - Prefer map/filter over manual loops
[ ] **Output consistent** - All code paths return same structure
